read_by: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and release decision
input: USFS FSim conditional flame-length class (RDS-2016-0034-3, 270 m), exact integer 1 to 6 (0 = no-event control); a class, not equipment heat flux
not_covered: Turbine fire assembly: blades, nacelle, tower (withheld, not zero)
Collection network, GSU main transformer, GSU switchgear and bus, GSU cable terminations (withheld)
Control, met-station and O&M buildings; foundation; civil (withheld)
Fieldwork and transport support (allocated once after repair scope; no fragility)
out_of_scope: Internal turbine or electrical fire, lightning and maintenance fires
Business interruption, revenue, PSPS and shutdown
missing_mechanisms: Firebrand attack and destructive residue or soot (separate deferred pathways)
Mitigation or clearance credit and operating state (captured, no numeric effect)

how_to_use.share_of: Direct replacement value of the same named unit (one pad's electrical equipment, or the one shared GSU protection-control-DC package)

outputs.single_event: conditional: exact FSim product ID, exact integer class 1 to 6, and the Tier-4 screening assumption-set ID
outputs.scenario_dollars: conditional: only with an explicit same-unit replacement value and local exposure fraction
outputs.yearly_loss: withheld for this partial screening release

conditions: Non-integer, unknown or out-of-range classes are rejected
No full-project TIV, mixed 72 USD/kW row or whole-farm damage ratio
The shared GSU package is counted once
Covered value share not stated by the cell; the mixed 72 USD/kW electrical row must be split by the site

method.summary: Cell-local Tier-4 screening points per FSim flame-length class, adopted under owner direction; research supports the mechanism and relative ordering, not the numbers

key_sources: USFS, Spatial datasets of probabilistic wildfire risk components for the US (270 m), 3rd ed., RDS-2016-0034-3 (2023) (WW1-S001)
Assessing wildfire risk to critical infrastructure in central Chile: an electrical substation, Int. J. Wildland Fire (2024) (WW1-S002)
NEMA GD 2-2016, Evaluating Fire- and Heat-Damaged Electrical Equipment (WW1-S003)
USFS, Wildfire vulnerability of power transmission and distribution infrastructure (2015) (WW1-S004)
Owner direction to represent wildfire-wind risk for one or two subsystems (WW1-A001; business decision)
judgment: Pad electrical damage points per flame-length class are a Tier-4 screening assumption
GSU protection-control-DC damage points per flame-length class are a Tier-4 screening assumption
Non-integer and out-of-range classes are rejected rather than interpolated
open_items: Validated bridge from FSim class to the heat and firebrand attack an asset actually receives
Inspected repair-or-replace outcomes and same-unit costs
Exogenous fire separated from internal, lightning and maintenance fires
No curve yet for the turbine fire assembly or the other GSU parts

rows.shape_basis: Tier-4 point array per flame-length class
rows.cost_basis: Same T4 point array sets the damage level as a share of the unit's value; no separate cost table

notes.text: Numbers match a wildfire_solar profile; the cell treats that as an audit comparison only

rows.shape_basis: Tier-4 point array per flame-length class; T3 support for ranking controls above steel-enclosed gear
rows.cost_basis: Same T4 point array sets the damage level as a share of the unit's value; no separate cost table

notes.text: One shared package per site, counted once
